title: Building Agents (the hard parts!) - Rita Kozlov, Cloudflare
talk_summary: A Cloudflare product talk framing agents as four components (client, reasoning, workflows, tools) and pitching their Agents SDK and Durable Objects for hosting MCP servers with built-in state. The only genuinely transferable engineering ideas are durable state for long-running/human-in-the-loop workflows and idempotency guards against duplicate actions.

takeaways.technique: Durable state for long-running, resumable workflows
takeaways.what_they_do: Workflows that pause on slow LLM calls or human approval are backed by a stateful primitive (Durable Objects) so the flow can resume exactly where it stopped instead of holding a process open.
takeaways.evidence_quote: you need something that's going to be able to come back and resume its flow after that task is completed
if two things happen out of sync, we can't approve the card twice

takeaways.technique: MCP server as shared tool surface with persistent memory
takeaways.what_they_do: Expose tools/resources/prompts via a standalone MCP server so multiple clients share the same tools and persisted state across sessions.
takeaways.evidence_quote: the memory is actually going to persist regardless of the tool that you're using to call into it

takeaways.technique: Ship prompts inside the tool/server definition
takeaways.what_they_do: MCP servers expose 'prompts' so the domain owner encodes interaction nuances where the tool lives, rather than in each client.
takeaways.evidence_quote: you can actually prompt your agent probably better than anyone else can
